title: Split live, golden, and results page scripts into client modules
description:
Several website pages are still carrying large inline scripts directly inside `.astro` files instead of using smaller reusable client modules.

Current hotspots:
- `website/src/pages/season/[season]/results.astro` is 1353 lines and includes inline JS for bracket resizing plus a large tournament game-card renderer.
- `website/src/pages/golden/[...slug].astro` is 1076 lines and contains a full standalone replay viewer bootstrap inline.
- `website/src/pages/games/live.astro` is 349 lines and still inlines the polling/render loop for the live viewer.

Why this matters:
- These pages are harder to review, test, and reuse because markup, CSS, data loading, and client behavior are interleaved.
- Inline page scripts make it easier for behavior to drift between pages that should share the same viewer primitives.
- Astro's bundling/module system is underused when large behavior blocks stay embedded in page files.

Suggested fix:
1. Move each large inline script into `website/src/scripts/` entry modules.
2. Keep the `.astro` pages thin: load data, render structure, import a small bootstrap.
3. Pull reusable DOM/viewer helpers into shared modules instead of leaving page-specific copies.

The goal is not just line-count reduction. The goal is to stop treating each page as a one-off JS app embedded in Astro.
